issue.title: sase monitor start handoff is silently lost when the provider turn ends mid-start
issue.description: On a host where 'sase monitor start' takes >20s (athena: 23-68s measured on ~40 overnight starts), codex hands control back while the command is in flight, the model ends its turn per the sase_monitor skill wording, and the provider exit kills the start before the supervisor acknowledges. No monitor record or pending marker exists (intent is persisted only after ack via persist_monitor_start_intent_after_ack), the sase-11t gate-intent guard is not used by the monitor module, and the codex turn-integrity check (_CodexTurnIntegrityState.integrity_error) passes any non-empty final message. The declaration-recovery turn then records the run as a clean success. Observed twice overnight 2026-09-17: sase-11y.2.1.5.land (23:26 EDT) and sase-11l.5.1.land--1 (03:19 EDT), both land continuations whose job was to close parent epics; both needed manual intervention (03:16, 06:18). Fix direction: write a .sase_handoff_intent.monitor file with full argv as the first action; runner replays an unconsumed intent or fails the run HandoffLost; treat any pending handoff command at turn end as an integrity failure; reword the skill to forbid ending the turn mid-start.

task_type_fields.impact: Land continuations that close parent epics vanish silently; epics stall for hours until a human notices (2 of ~40 athena monitor starts lost in one night, ~7h of combined epic delay)
task_type_fields.repro: Run a codex agent that invokes 'sase monitor start' on a slow-start host (athena) and ends its turn within ~20s of the call yielding; the start dies pre-ack, no monitor exists, and the run is reported completed
